reuse.why: Ignores the existing shared getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts and writes the amount rule inline twice, only reusing getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance.

duplication.why: The same null/number/range dispatch with tolerance arithmetic is written separately in api-models.ts and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, alongside the untouched midpoint copies in forecast-schedules, schedules/app.ts (two) and schedule-template.

placement.why: Planning-amount logic is put inline in the API model mapper and inside the preview function instead of in the shared amount helper that the client and server already import.

scope.why: Touches only the API mapper and preview, so it is small, but it leaves most of the paths the request's rule governs (posting, rule actions, forecast, budget template, getScheduledAmount for the UI) unchanged.

maintainability.why: The two inline copies already disagree (the API uses the furthest-from-zero rule of step 3 with Math.sign, the preview the lowest-value rule of step 4), and the other sites still use the midpoint, so the rule now has three versions.

bypasses_abstraction.where: api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal and shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions compute the expected amount inline instead of through getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The API copy (Math.abs comparison, Math.sign * threshold) and the preview copy (num1 <= num2, -threshold) are reshaped versions of the same dispatch that also exists in getScheduledAmount.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount is not changed; api-models.ts scheduleModel and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions re-implement the rule inline, while forecast-schedules normalizeSchedule, schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, and budget/schedule-template keep their own midpoint copies.
